In exchange for the coterie's intelligence on Tzimisce shipping at the docks, the Camarilla sanctioned their territorial claim over the West Covina Church domain.

entries.title: CS Volga Spirit Incident
entries.content: A major maritime intelligence operation at the Port of Los Angeles (WBCT Berth 09). The Russian container ship CS Volga Spirit arrived from Vladivostok carrying container 090482, loaded with six bulk polypropylene bags of native soil from Tzimisce homelands, fraudulent identity papers, and a classified German police report linking identical bite-mark homicides across 80 years, proving a direct Camarilla Masquerade breach.

entries.title: Daylight Assassination of Jade Nguyen
entries.content: A catastrophic breach and tragedy in Downtown Los Angeles. Jade Nguyen, an aspiring young actress and Toreador/Ventrue ghoul close to Elliot 'Shane' Mercer, was executed in broad daylight by an elite mortal sniper team outside the Stellaris Conservatory. The assassination confirmed that organized mortal hunter cells (First Light / SAD) are operating with advanced military weaponry within the city.

entries.title: Fall of House Crimson Sigils
entries.content: A devastating assault by Sabbat shock troops against the Tremere chantry of House Crimson Sigils. Led by Archbishop Delacroix, Marcus 'Ironfist', and a massive fleshcrafted Vozhd, the Sabbat shattered the exterior ward stones. Sentinel Gareth MacDougal and the 200-year-old granite Gargoyle Stoneheart made a bloody final stand in the great foyer before the chantry was entirely annihilated.
entries.source: The Last Stand at House Crimson Sigils.json

entries.title: Harrison Residence Fleshcrafting Horror
entries.content: A horrifying scene investigated by Balthazar in South Central. Tzimisce fleshcrafter Arsenio Hall confiscated the suburban home of the mortal Harrison family, mutilating them into structural biological traps and keeping a dormant Vozhd alongside shotgun-wielding fleshcrafted sentinels in a reinforced subterranean vault.

entries.title: Lynn Ranch Abduction & Extraction
entries.content: A high-stakes tactical raid in the equestrian hills near Thousand Oaks. Reverend Frederik King was ambushed and captured on the church grounds by Lasombra shadow-wielder Rafael de Andueza and Bishop Sébastién Debs. After being held at the fortified Lynn Ranch Sabbat compound, Frederik was liberated in a synchronized assault by the coterie, leaving the enemy safehouse heavily damaged by fire.

entries.title: Neon Temple Street Riot
entries.content: A volatile midnight brawl outside the Neon Temple club in Hollywood. Over twenty vampires clashed on the street, pitting Anarch leaders Jeremy MacNeil and Smiling Jack against Antifa-styled Caitiff agitators waving red-and-black flags. The melee escalated into gunfire when a rooftop sniper with the Quietus discipline opened fire, drawing immediate LAPD attention.

entries.title: Operation Bayside Blue
entries.content: A high-precision luxury vehicle heist executed in Palos Verdes Estates. Orchestrated by Liam Johnson, the coterie breached the cliffside mansion of paranoid crypto-millionaire Devon 'Vandal' Vance, evading motion-tracking security cameras to liberate a pristine, factory-original Bayside Blue Nissan Skyline GT-R (R34) for South Central smuggler contacts.

entries.title: Status Perfectus (The Perfect State)
entries.content: The historic 1944 revolutionary manifesto drafted by the Los Angeles Revolutionary Council following the fall of Don Sebastian. It codified the principles of the Anarch Free State: absolute rejection of elder hegemony, mutual defense regardless of clan, popular accountability for Barons, and the spiritual sanctity of Kindred libertas.

entries.title: West Covina Bastion Fortification
entries.content: The systematic engineering of the former Presbyterian church in West Covina into an impregnable Haven for the coterie. Funded by $400k in foundational backing and $15k in debris clearance, the site features two subterranean bunker floors, four concentric defensive rings of gasoline and explosives laid by George Michael, and a natural gas connection to explain away potential explosions.

entries.title: Anarch Free State Council
entries.content: The decentralized alliance of territorial Barons, neighborhood warlords, and revolutionary veterans presiding over the greater Los Angeles basin. Anchored by figures like Jeremy MacNeil, Nines Rodriguez (Downtown), and Victor Temple, the council struggles to balance libertarian freedom against encroaching Camarilla embassies and violent Sabbat incursions.

entries.title: Bar Afterlife & Rams Syndicate
entries.content: The primary philosophical and tactical center for Downtown Kindred, located on Central Avenue. Managed by Brujah Primogen Salvador Garcia alongside Seneschal 'Big' Ed Hurley, the sports bar doubles as an intense game-day sanctuary for LA Rams fans and a neutral ground for political arbitration between Anarch ancillae and Camarilla diplomats.

entries.title: Camarilla Court of Los Angeles
entries.content: The sovereign Ivory Tower administration maintaining a precarious, heavily armed foothold across the metropolitan area. Governed from the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion by Ventrue Prince Meredith Vereira, the court relies on Seneschal Ed Hurley, Sheriff Anthohimondrona Tsuoranoannddy, Keeper Amanda Byers, and Harpy Audrey Horne to enforce the Traditions.

entries.title: Clan Tremere Chantry of the Angels
entries.content: The official Camarilla chantry in Los Angeles, currently grappling with occult instability and security paranoia following the catastrophic destruction of House Crimson Sigils. Its Hermetic sorcerers aggressively monitor unusual magical surges and black-market relic trading.

entries.title: Latin Kings Auto Theft Network
entries.content: A powerful South Central street and auto-smuggling syndicate liaised by David Martinez and senior operative Hernando Fabregas. The organization works closely with Liam Johnson to fence exotic stolen vehicles, procure untraceable transport, and provide street-level muscle.

entries.title: Mortal Hunter Enclave (First Light / SAD)
entries.content: A lethal, highly coordinated cell of mortal witch-hunters and government special agents operating covertly within Los Angeles. Led by tactical operatives like Erica '5ynaps3' Milton, Sir Isaac Townsend, Joshua Preston, and Jacob Singer, the cell demonstrated its reach with the daylight sniper assassination of Jade Nguyen.

entries.title: Sabbat Simi Valley / Lynn Ranch Diocese
entries.content: A violent, covert Sword of Caine cell entrenched in Thousand Oaks, Simi Valley, and the northern hills. Led by Lasombra Bishop Sébastién Debs, shadow-infiltrator Rafael de Andueza, and Irina Kozlov, the pack specializes in grave looting, psychological terror, and haven raids.

entries.title: The Sabbat Sire Syndicate
entries.content: The chilling revelation uncovered by the coterie that their respective sires—Clayton White, Philip Zambardo, and Keith Brown—are not merely rogue elders, but high-ranking Sabbat ideologues and operational architects running deep-cover infiltration missions across Los Angeles.

entries.title: West Covina Flock (Church of the New Dawn)
entries.content: Reverend Frederik King's rapidly expanding mortal congregation and veteran community. Based at the renovated West Covina sanctuary, the flock is administered by ghouls John Carmac and George Michael with pastoral coordination by Mrs. Martha Gable, giving the coterie an impassioned mortal shield and loyal herd.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Balthazar
entries.content: A battle-hardened, intensely paranoid former Camarilla sheriff and enforcer. Driven by an obsessive vendetta against Tzimisce fleshcrafters and Sabbat sleeper agents, Balthazar constantly rotates through hidden safehouses to avoid surveillance while conducting brutal interrogations.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Bernard Tulle ('DJ Warlock')
entries.content: An Auspex-gifted occult specialist and techno-shaman allied with Balthazar. Operating under the alias 'DJ Warlock', Bernard uses his psychic sensitivities (Spirit's Touch) and dockside connections to inspect suspect cargo containers and monitor occult artifacts.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Chris Partlow
entries.content: A disciplined, stone-faced retired soldier bound as a trusted ghoul to Elliot 'Shane' Mercer. Partlow provides professional executive protection, surveillance detection, and military discipline, ensuring Shane's artistic pursuits remain secure from street interference.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Clayton White
entries.content: An 8th Generation Brujah and sire of Liam Johnson. An emancipated slave from 1870 harboring an enduring hatred for white racial institutions, Clayton operates as a formidable revolutionary architect in the Sabbat, selecting Liam after spotting him stealing vehicles from neo-Nazis.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Elliot 'Shane' Mercer
entries.content: 8th Generation Toreador player character. Formerly a neglected street urchin, Shane rose to prominence as a brilliant modern artist and cultural icon. His unlife was shattered by the daylight sniper assassination of his beloved ghoul Jade, driving him toward vengeance.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Frederic King
entries.content: 8th Generation Malkavian player character. An excommunicated Amish preacher whose divine delusions and potent Dementation led him to found the Church of the New Dawn in West Covina, where he presides over a devoted flock under a solemn vow of silence.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: George Michael
entries.content: An Amish military combat veteran suffering from severe PTSD, now bound as a devoted ghoul to Frederic King. George manages the coterie's heavy firearms, defensive explosive rings, and tactical fortifications around the West Covina church property.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Isabel Turner
entries.content: 8th Generation Ventrue player character. A sharp, elegant corporate litigator and estate strategist maneuvering through high-society boardrooms. She balances domain politics while shielding her dominated mortal husband Kevin from predatory elder schemes.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Jade Nguyen (In Memoriam)
entries.content: An aspiring young actress and Toreador/Ventrue ghoul studying at the Stellaris Conservatory, deeply beloved by Shane Mercer. Her brutal daylight assassination by mortal snipers in Downtown Los Angeles catalyzed the coterie's investigation into citywide hunter networks.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: John Carmac
entries.content: A savvy modern Amish marketing freelancer bound as a primary ghoul to Frederic King. John manages the daytime bureaucracy, banking accounts, contractor negotiations, and public relations for the Church of the New Dawn.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Katrine Sterling
entries.content: A disgraced aerospace drone technician and skilled hacker bound as a ghoul to Frederic King. She oversees electronic warfare, forensic camera scrubbing, encrypted communications, and aerial drone surveillance for the coterie.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Keith Brown
entries.content: An 8th Generation Ventrue and sire of Isabel Turner. Known publicly as an executive producer of gritty grindhouse films, Keith is secretly a major Sabbat media mogul pulling strings behind independent production houses and cinematic distribution.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Liam Johnson ('L.J.')
entries.content: 8th Generation Brujah player character. An elite wheelman and criminal GTA specialist with 5 dots in Drive and potent Celerity. Liam won his signature muscle car in a street race against Hector and maintains close ties with the Latin Kings auto theft syndicate.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Mrs. Martha Gable
entries.content: A warm, devout mortal matriarch and church volunteer coordinator managing prayer chains, food drives, and charity bake sales at the Church of the New Dawn. She reveres Frederik King as a holy, ascetic man of God recovering from a severe spiritual trial.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Philip Zambardo
entries.content: An 8th Generation Malkavian and sire of Frederic King. A disgraced academic psychologist involved in the Stanford prison experiment, Zambardo was Embraced late in natural life and is feared within the Sabbat as 'The Hollow Saint' for his terrifying psychological conditioning.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Princess Donna Delore
entries.content: An 8th Generation Toreador and sire of Shane Mercer. Embraced in the early 1980s, Donna made a fortune producing early home video and adult films before reinventing herself as an elite body artist, now operating an exclusive tattoo haven in Arcadia.

entries.section: LA Campaign: The Coterie & Inner Circle
entries.title: Rachel Teller
entries.content: An exceptionally beautiful and resourceful woman bound as a loyal ghoul to Liam Johnson. She assists Liam with surveillance, target scouting, and liaison work across Los Angeles.

entries.title: Arcadia Tattoo Parlor
entries.content: Princess Donna Delore's vibrant, warded studio and haven in Arcadia. Combining neon aesthetics, sacred geometry, and high-end artistic tattoo equipment, it serves as a secure sanctuary where Toreador artists and discreet guests congregate.

entries.title: Bar Afterlife
entries.content: A high-end sports bar and lounge on Central Avenue in Downtown Los Angeles. Featuring dark brick, leather booths, and an intimate backroom, it serves as Salvador Garcia's philosophical salon and the primary rallying hub for passionate LA Rams tailgaters.

entries.title: Church of the New Dawn (West Covina Bastion)
entries.content: The coterie's fortified primary haven in West Covina, situated on a former Presbyterian church property. Engineered with two reinforced subterranean bunker crypts, heavy blast doors, and concentric defensive fuel trenches, all masked behind an active Christian ministry.

entries.title: Dorothy Chandler Pavilion
entries.content: The grand, sweeping cultural centerpiece of Downtown Los Angeles. Built with glass, polished marble, and crystal chandeliers, it operates as Prince Meredith Vereira's primary formal Elysium under the protection of the Pax Vampirica.

entries.title: Iron Curtain Bunker & Silver Lake Laundromat
entries.content: The subterranean Haven and electronic listening post of Nosferatu Primogen Silas 'Root' Thorne. Concealed behind a commercial laundromat in Silver Lake, the facility houses air-gapped mainframes monitoring traffic cameras, telephone trunks, and municipal telemetry.

entries.title: Lynn Ranch Compound
entries.content: A secluded equestrian property nestled in the hills near Thousand Oaks and the Ventura County line. Utilized by Sabbat Bishop Sébastién Debs and Rafael de Andueza as an interrogation base and safehouse until heavily scorched during the coterie's rescue raid.

entries.title: Neon Temple
entries.content: A pulsing, multi-tier industrial gothic nightclub in Hollywood. Known for ear-shattering electronic music, strobe-lit dance floors, and private VIP lounges, it serves as a premier hunting ground for fledglings, ghouls, and Anarch youth.

entries.title: Pinnacle Vault Gallery
entries.content: An ultra-modern, fortified art gallery on Camden Drive in Beverly Hills constructed from black granite and tempered glass. Owned and curated for exclusive Toreador exhibitions, high-stakes auctions (Ewald Borsod), and private Kindred diplomacy.

entries.title: The Bleeding Heart
entries.content: A discrete, low-lit gentlemen's club in West Covina. Operating well into the early morning hours, it serves as the coterie's primary local feeding ground and suburban rumor mill after 3:00 AM.

entries.title: WBCT Berth 09 (Port of Los Angeles)
entries.content: A massive deep-water shipping berth at the West Basin Container Terminal in San Pedro. Dominated by towering gantry cranes and endless stacks of shipping containers, it was the site of the CS Volga Spirit interception.

mechanics.title: Combat Systems
mechanics.content:
# Appendix — Combat Systems & Maneuvers (V20 Core)

Source: **V20 Core Rulebook** Chapter Six: Systems and Drama, pp. 271–281. Light
format: turn structure, initiative, attack, maneuvers, damage resolution, armor,
and weapons. Combat rules are guidelines — the Storyteller is the final arbiter.

## Types of combat (p. 271)

- **Close combat** — unarmed (Dexterity + Brawl; within 1 yard/m) and melee
  (Dexterity + Melee; within 2 yards/m).
- **Ranged combat** — projectile weapons (Dexterity + Firearms for guns,
  Dexterity + Athletics for thrown); needs sight and range.

## Combat turns (pp. 271–273)

Combat is divided into **three-second turns**, each with three stages:

**Stage One: Initiative**
- Roll **one die** and add it to the **initiative rating (Dexterity + Wits)**;
  Celerity adds its dots to Dexterity-related rolls, including initiative
  (confirmed by the example of play, p. 302). Highest total acts first.
- **Everyone declares their actions** in reverse order of initiative; actions
  may be delayed to any later point in the order.
- **Declare multiple actions** (splitting pools) at this stage, and **declare
  Discipline activation and Willpower expenditure**.
- Actions can be **aborted** to a defensive action (block/dodge/parry) at any
  time before the character acts, via a successful Willpower roll (diff 6) or by
  spending 1 WP.
- **Yielding**: a character may allow the next-highest initiative to act; if
  everyone yields, nothing happens that turn.

**Stage Two: Attack**
- Unarmed: Dexterity + Brawl. Melee: Dexterity + Melee. Ranged: Dexterity +
  Firearms (or Athletics for thrown).
- **Each extra success on the attack roll adds one automatic die to the damage
  dice pool** (the "cinematic" combat escalator).

**Stage Three: Resolution**
- Determine total damage effect (weapon type or maneuver) plus the extra dice
  from attack successes.
- **Targets may attempt to soak** (reflexive, no pool split).

## Damage types (p. 272)

- **Bashing** — punches, clubs, blunt trauma; vs mortals soaked with full
  Stamina; marked with "/".
- **Lethal** — knives, bullets, swords; mortals may NOT soak it; vampires soak
  with Stamina; marked with "X".
- **Aggravated** — fire, sunlight, teeth and claws of vampires/werewolves/
  supernaturals; **soakable only with Fortitude**; marked with "*".
- Damage dice pools can never drop below **1 die**. Damage and soak rolls
  **cannot botch** — a "botch" damage roll just glances harmlessly.

## Soak (p. 272)

- Soak pool = **Stamina** (+ **Fortitude** against bashing and lethal; against
  aggravated, **only Fortitude**).
- Soak is **reflexive** (no action, no pool split). Default difficulty **6**.
- Each soak success subtracts one die's worth of damage. Soak rolls only fail,
  never botch.

## Armor (pp. 272, 280)

- Armor **adds its rating to the soak dice pool** against bashing, lethal, and
  aggravated (from teeth/claws). **No protection vs fire or sunlight.**
- Armor is destroyed if a single attack's damage roll equals **twice the armor's
  rating**.
- Armor penalty subtracts dice from Dexterity-based pools.
- Targeting unprotected areas (typically +1 or +2 difficulty) bypasses armor.

| Class | Rating | Penalty |
|---|---|---|
| Class One (reinforced clothing) | 1 | 0 |
| Class Two (armor T-shirt) | 2 | 1 |
| Class Three (Kevlar vest) | 3 | 1 |
| Class Four (flak jacket) | 4 | 2 |
| Class Five (full riot gear) | 5 | 3 |

## General maneuvers (p. 274)

- **Aborting actions** — drop your declared action for block/dodge/parry if you
  haven't acted yet; needs a Willpower roll (diff 6) or 1 WP (declared at abort).
- **Ambush** — Dexterity + Stealth (resisted) vs Perception + Alertness; win =
  one free attack, extra successes added to the attack pool; tie = attacker still
  first but target may defend; target win = spotted, normal initiative. Targets
  already in combat can't be ambushed.
- **Blind fighting** — +2 difficulty; ranged attacks can't be made accurately at
  all (Heightened Senses, Eyes of the Beast mitigate).
- **Flank attacks** +1 attack die; **rear attacks** +2 attack dice.
- **Movement** — move up to half running speed and still act; each yard moved
  while acting subtracts 1 die from that action.
- **Targeting** — aim for a specific location: +1 diff (medium: limb, briefcase,
  no damage mod); +2 diff (small: hand, head — +1 damage); +3 diff (precise:
  eye, heart — +2 damage).
- **Multiple opponents** — +1 difficulty (cumulative, max +4) to attack AND
  defend per extra opponent.

## Defensive maneuvers (pp. 274–275)

All are **resisted against the attack roll** — the attacker needs more successes
than the defender to hit; the defender's successes reduce the attacker's net
successes even if she can't fully stop the attack. Declare any time before the
attacker rolls, if you have an action left (or abort).

- **Block** — Dexterity + Brawl; body deflects a hand-to-hand **bashing** attack
  only; lethal/aggravated need Fortitude or armor.
- **Dodge** — Dexterity + Athletics; avoids any attack type. No room to maneuver
  → must block/parry. Vs gunfire: move ≥1 yard and get behind cover (or drop
  prone); cover rules then apply.
- **Parry** — Dexterity + Melee; uses a weapon vs Brawl/Melee. If the parry beats
  the attacker's successes, the attacker may take the weapon's base damage plus
  the parry's extra successes.
- **Full defense turn** — don't split pools; first defense uses full pool, each
  subsequent defense −1 die cumulative.

## Close combat maneuvers (pp. 275–276)

| Maneuver | Traits | Accuracy | Difficulty | Damage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bite | Dex + Brawl | +1 | Normal | Str +1 (aggravated) |
| Block | Dex + Brawl | Special | Normal | None (reduces attack) |
| Claw | Dex + Brawl | Normal | Normal | Str +1 (aggravated if Feral Claws) |
| Clinch | Str + Brawl | Normal | Normal | Str (carries over turns) |
| Disarm | Dex + Melee | Normal | +1 | Special |
| Dodge | Dex + Athletics | Special | Normal | None (reduces attack) |
| Hold | Str + Brawl | Normal | Normal | None (carries over) |
| Kick | Dex + Brawl | Normal | +1 | Str +1 |
| Parry | Dex + Melee | Special | Normal | None (reduces attack) |
| Strike | Dex + Brawl | Normal | Normal | Str |
| Sweep | Dex + Brawl/Melee | Normal | +1 | Str + knockdown |
| Tackle | Str + Brawl | Normal | +1 | Str +1 + knockdown |
| Weapon Strike | Dex + Melee | Normal | Normal | Weapon |

Details:
- **Bite / Kiss**: A bite needs a successful clinch/hold/tackle first, then bites
  next turn; aggravated. A **Kiss** does no damage but lets the vampire drain
  blood at the normal rate (victim usually helpless); the wound can be licked
  closed.
- **Claw**: aggravated if from Feral Claws; lethal if Vicissitude-constructed.
- **Clinch**: first turn Strength damage; each subsequent turn either Strength
  damage automatically or escape via resisted **Strength + Brawl**.
- **Hold**: immobilizes until the target wins a resisted Strength + Brawl.
- **Sweep**: target rolls **Dexterity + Athletics (diff 8)** or is knocked down.
- **Tackle**: both parties roll **Dexterity + Athletics (diff 7)** or knockdown;
  even a successful target is at +1 difficulty next turn.
- **Disarm**: attack at +1 difficulty; if successes exceed the opponent's
  Strength, no damage but they're disarmed. Botch = you drop your weapon or get
  hit.
- **Weapon length**: a shorter-weapon attacker must close 1 yard (losing 1 die).

## Ranged combat maneuvers (pp. 277–278)

| Maneuver | Traits | Accuracy | Difficulty | Damage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aiming | — | +1/turn (max Perception) | Normal | — |
| Automatic Fire | Dex + Firearms | +10 | +2 | Special |
| Multiple Shots | Dex + Firearms | Special | Normal | Weapon |
| Strafing | Dex + Firearms | +10 | +2 | Special |
| Three-Round Burst | Dex + Firearms | +2 | +1 | Weapon |
| Two Weapons | Dex + Firearms | Normal | +1 (off-hand) | Weapon |

- **Aiming** — +1 die per turn spent aiming, max = Perception (Firearms 1+
  required; a scope adds +2 on the first turn). Can't aim at a target moving
  faster than a walk.
- **Automatic fire** — unloads the clip on one target: +10 accuracy, +2
  difficulty (recoil), damage treated as one bullet; clip must be ≥ half full;
  can't target specific body areas.
- **Cover** — light (prone) +1, good (behind wall) +2, superior (only head
  exposed) +3 to hit; firing back from cover is −1 difficulty vs listed; cover
  penalties are cumulative between combatants.
- **Range** — difficulty 6 at short range; difficulty 8 out to twice the listed
  range; **point blank (≤2 m) = difficulty 4**.
- **Reloading** — one full turn (can be part of a multiple action).
- **Strafing** — +10 accuracy, empties the clip over up to 3 yards; successes
  divided among targets; Dodge vs strafing at +1 difficulty.
- **Three-round burst** — +2 dice, +1 difficulty (recoil), 3 shots, damage of
  one bullet.
- **Two weapons** — multiple action (split lowest pool) + +1 difficulty off-hand
  (unless ambidextrous).

## Maneuver complications (pp. 278–279)

- **Blinded** — +2 dice to hit a blinded target; a blinded character is at +2
  difficulty on all actions.
- **Dazed** — if damage successes exceed the target's Stamina (mortal) or
  Stamina + 2 (vampire/supernatural), the victim must spend her next turn shaking
  it off. Only soak-penetrating successes count.
- **Immobilization** — +2 dice to hit an immobilized-but-struggling target;
  attacks auto-hit a completely immobilized target.
- **Knockdown** — Dexterity + Athletics: success = get up (initiative −2 next
  turn); failure = spend next action rising; botch = 1 automatic bashing.
- **Stake Through Heart** — target the heart (**difficulty 9**); 3+ health levels
  of damage immobilizes a vampire (conscious, Auspex usable, can't move or spend
  blood) until the stake is removed.

## Weapons (p. 280)

**Melee:**
| Weapon | Damage | Conceal |
|---|---|---|
| Sap+ | Str +1 | P (pocket) |
| Club+ | Str +2 | T (trenchcoat) |
| Knife | Str +1 | J (jacket) |
| Sword | Str +2 | T |
| Axe | Str +3 | N (none) |
| Stake* | Str +1 | T |

+ Blunt objects inflict bashing unless head-targeted (then lethal).
* May paralyze a vampire through the heart (diff 9, 3 damage successes).

**Ranged** (Damage / Range / Rate / Capacity / Conceal):
- Revolver, Lt. (SW Bodyguard .38) 4 / 12 / 3 / 6 / P
- Revolver, Hvy. (Ruger Redhawk .44) 6 / 35 / 2 / 6 / J
- Pistol, Lt. (HK USP 9mm) 4 / 20 / 4 / 15+1 / P
- Pistol, Hvy. (Springfield XDM .45) 5 / 25 / 3 / 13+1 / J
- Rifle (Beretta Tikka T3 30.06) 8 / 200 / 1 / 3+1 / N
- SMG, Small (Glock 18)* 4 / 20 / 3 / 17+1 / J
- SMG, Large (HK MP5)* 4 / 50 / 3 / 30+1 / T
- Assault Rifle (FN SCAR)* 7 / 150 / 3 / 30+1 / N
- Shotgun (Remington 870) 8 / 20 / 1 / 5+1 / T
- Shotgun, Semi-auto (Benelli M4) 8 / 20 / 3 / 6+1 / T
- Crossbow** 5 / 20 / 1 / 1 / T

* Capable of 3-round burst, full-auto, and spray. ** For staking; 5-turn
reload; bashing vs Kindred unless aimed at head/heart, lethal vs mortals.

**Firearms vs vampires:** considered **bashing** unless the head is targeted
(difficulty 8), then **lethal**. Vs mortals, always lethal.

mechanics.title: Damage, Health & Blood
mechanics.content:
# Appendix — Damage, Soak, Health, Blood Pool, Willpower (V20 Core)

Source: **V20 Core Rulebook** Chapter Six: Systems and Drama, pp. 266–295. Light
format: cost, pool, difficulty, and effect. This appendix covers the Scholar's
**resource economy** — blood, Willpower, health, and damage — which interacts
with every Discipline power in Parts I–IV.

## Damage types (pp. 272, 284)

Three types; applied to the Health chart in order: aggravated on top, lethal
below it, bashing below that (aggravated always marked above lethal above
bashing; normal damage is marked last and heals first).

| Type | Mark | Soak (mortal) | Soak (vampire) | Healing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bashing | / | full Stamina | Stamina (+ Fortitude), then **halved** (round down) | fast |
| Lethal | X | none | Stamina (+ Fortitude) | blood (1 BP/level) |
| Aggravated | * | (treated as lethal) | **only Fortitude** | 5 BP + full day rest |

- Damage dice pools never drop below **1 die**; damage and soak rolls can't
  botch.
- **Firearms vs vampires** = bashing unless head-targeted (diff 8), then lethal.
- Incapacitated + more bashing/lethal → **torpor**; Incapacitated + aggravated →
  **Final Death**.

## Soak (p. 272)

Soak pool = **Stamina**, plus **Fortitude** vs bashing/lethal; **only Fortitude**
vs aggravated. Reflexive, default difficulty **6**, each success subtracts one die
of damage. Never botches, only fails.

## Health levels (pp. 282–283)

Seven levels: Bruised, Hurt, Injured, Wounded, Mauled, Crippled, Incapacitated.

| Health Level | Dice Pool Penalty | Movement |
|---|---|---|
| Bruised | 0 | none |
| Hurt | −1 | none |
| Injured | −1 | halve max running speed |
| Wounded | −2 | may not run (walk only); move *or* attack, not both |
| Mauled | −2 | hobble 3 yds/m per turn |
| Crippled | −5 | crawl 1 yd/m per turn |
| Incapacitated | — | no movement; only spend blood to heal |

The wound penalty subtracts from every action pool **except reflexive actions**
such as soak. **Incapacitated**: collapses; further damage → torpor (or Final
Death if aggravated). **Torpor**: deathlike trance, cannot act or spend blood.

**Torpor length** (from wounds) by Humanity/Path: 10 = 1 day; 9 = 3 days; 8 =
1 week; 7 = 2 weeks; 6 = 1 month; 5 = 1 year; 4 = 1 decade; 3 = 5 decades; 2 =
1 century; 1 = 5 centuries; 0 = millennium+. Rise requires a **Perception
(diff 8)** roll to notice disturbances and a **Humanity/Path (diff 8)** roll to
wake; each success = 1 turn of activity, 5 = fully awake for the scene. A vampire
woken from torpor is at **Crippled** and must feed or spend blood immediately.
Voluntary torpor: half the mandatory time, needs an Awakening roll.

**Optional rule — Extras**: nameless STC thugs get only 4 health levels (Hurt −1,
Maimed −3, Incapacitated, Dead).

## Vampire healing (pp. 268, 285)

- **Bashing/lethal**: spend **1 blood point per health level**, 1 BP per turn
  (or more per turn by Generation). Requires concentration/rest — healing while
  acting needs a reflexive **Stamina + Survival (diff 8)**; failure wastes the
  blood, botch also costs an extra BP + an extra health level.
- **Aggravated**: a full day of rest + **5 blood points** per level; additional
  aggravated levels after the first day cost **5 BP + 1 Willpower** each.
- Blood is the **only** way vampires heal; they never recover naturally.

## Mortal healing times (pp. 285–286)

**Bashing** (Bruised to Wounded 1 hour; Maimed 3 hours; Crippled 6 hours;
Incapacitated 12 hours). **Lethal** (Bruised 1 day; Hurt 3 days; Injured 1 week;
Wounded 1 month; Maimed 2 months; Crippled 3 months; Incapacitated 5 months).
Untreated lethal wounds past Hurt worsen 1 level/day; Crippled/Incapacitated need
medical care to recover.

## Blood pool (pp. 268–270)

- Spend **1 BP every night** on rising (whether or not the vampire goes out).
- A vampire may spend only a **certain number of BP per turn** by Generation
  (the Scholar, 8th gen: **15 BP pool, 3 BP/turn** — established project canon).
- **Healing** = 1 BP per bashing/lethal level (see above).
- **Physical Attributes**: spend 1 BP to raise one Physical Attribute
  (Strength/Dexterity/Stamina) **+1 for the scene**, up to **one above the
  Generational max** (8th gen max 5 → freely up to 6). Each dot above the max
  lasts **3 turns** after blood stops being spent. **No attribute may exceed 10.**
  Spend up to the per-turn limit; announce at the start of the turn.
- **Disciplines** and **blood magic** fuel from the pool.
- **Appearing human**: spend (8 − Humanity) BP for a scene (automatic for
  Humanity 8+; Humanity-path only, not Paths).
- **Ghouls**: gifting vitae makes a mortal/animal a ghoul while it's in their
  system. **Blood bonds**: three drinks over three nights = a blood bond.
- **Feeding**: up to **3 BP per turn** from a vessel; a human holds 10 BP (take
  2 safely, 5 = hospitalization, 10 = death). The **Kiss** makes most victims
  helpless (Willpower 9+ may resist; Kindred can resist with **Self-Control/
  Instincts diff 8**).
- **Frenzy cap**: a Self-Control/Instincts roll may never use more dice than the
  character's **current blood pool**.

**Blood pool of vessels** (BP): vampire 10+, werewolf 20, average human 10,
child 5, cow 5, dog 2, cat 1, plasma bag 1, bird ½, bat/rat ¼. Wounded humans
hold 1 fewer BP per health level; they regain 1 BP/day.

**Elder/animal/werewolf blood**: elder or werewolf blood is so concentrated that
each BP taken may count as 2+ normal BP. Animal blood yields less than volume.

## Willpower (pp. 266–267)

Willpower has a **permanent rating** (rolled) and a **temporary pool** (spent).
The Scholar: **WP 5 / 5**.

**Spending:**
- **1 WP = 1 automatic success** on a single action (once per turn; cannot be
  canceled by botches; declared before rolling; ST may forbid on some actions).
- **1 WP** to avoid an instinctive/reactive action (leaping back from a chasm,
  sunlight, etc.).
- **1 WP** to suppress a derangement for a time (Malkavians can never overcome
  their initial one).
- **1 WP** to **ignore wound penalties for one turn** (incapacitated/torpid
  vampires can't).
- **1 WP** to abort to a defensive action in combat.

**Regaining:** pool refills fully at the **end of a story** (not session); ST
options: +1/night on rising, rewards for extraordinary goals, +1–3 for fulfilling
the Nature archetype. The pool can never exceed the rating; the rating rises only
with experience.

## Frenzy & Rötschreck (pp. 297–299)

**Frenzy** — the Beast takes over: ignore wound penalties until it ends; +2
difficulty to Dominate/mentally control a frenzied vampire (and −2 to resist such
control); immune to Rötschreck; no Willpower rolls needed.

- Resist with **Self-Control** (or Instincts) vs difficulty 6–8 (or **9 −
  Conscience** if the act is blatantly evil). **5 successes** = fully resist;
  fewer = resist 1 turn per success (re-roll to keep resisting); **failure** =
  frenzy; **botch** = frenzy until ST decides + possible derangement.
- During frenzy, 1 WP lets the player control one action for one turn.
- Frenzy difficulty by provocation: smell of blood (hungry) 3; sight of blood 4;
  harassment 4; life-threatening 4; malicious taunts 4; physical provocation 6;
  taste of blood 6; loved one in danger 7; public humiliation 8.

**Rötschreck (Red Fear)** — fear of fire/sunlight: resist with **Courage** (5
successes to fully ignore; fewer = overcome for a time). Failure = mad flight,
tearing through anything in the way; restraint triggers an attack; 1 WP controls
one action for a turn; botched Courage = frenzy until ST decides. Difficulty by
provocation: lighting a cigarette 3; sight of a torch 5; bonfire 6; obscured
sunlight 7; being burned 7; direct sunlight 8; trapped in a burning building 9.

## Sunlight & fire (pp. 296, 301–302)

- **Fire**: aggravated damage. Fortitude soaks; other vampires may frenzy from
  fire.
- **Sunlight**: aggravated; only **Fortitude** soaks (pool = Fortitude rating);
  difficulty and damage depend on light intensity and protection. Direct
  sunlight sears to ash; any vampire looking directly into it is **blinded
  instantly**. Diffuse/obscured sunlight still burns (Courage diff 7). Vampires
  submerged in shallow water have cloud-cover-equivalent protection.

## Blood bond (pp. 286–287)

Three drinks over three nights = full blood bond to the regnant.
- **1st drink**: strong feelings, no mechanical effect (all childer are 1-drink
  bonded to sires).
- **2nd drink**: behavior influence; Willpower roll needed for directly harmful
  actions; social rolls vs the thrall at −1 difficulty.
- **3rd drink**: full bond — regnant may Dominate the thrall **without eye
  contact** (voice is enough); the thrall resists mental control at +2
  difficulty (Generation limits still apply). Lesser bonds are wiped out.
- **Resisting**: Willpower roll (typically diff 8, max 9) accumulating successes
  equal to the number of drinks, then spend 1 WP; negates the bond for a scene
  (plotting) to a turn (physical attack).
- **Breaking**: no contact for **(12 × Willpower) months** reduces the bond one
  level; repeated reductions to zero unlink it. Killing the regnant shatters the
  bond (ST discretion on the aftermath).

## The Vaulderie / Vinculum (pp. 288–289)

Sabbat rite mixing all pack members' vitae; creates Vinculi (blood-ties), rated
1–10 per relationship. Ratings change on each rite (roll a die; higher than the
score = +1, a 1 = −1). Effects at 10 = willing to give/life take life; 9 = nearly
anything; 8 = resources/assistance; 7 = moderate risk, may kill for; 6 = fight
for; 5 = help if convenient; 4 = aid if no risk; 3 = loyalty that doesn't
interfere; 2 = minor kinship; 1 = don't care. Vinculi **never fade**; a Vaulderie
(with ≥1 BP left and 6 points of Vaulderie vitae drunk) can erode a blood bond,
but blood bonds can't easily erase Vinculi.

## Diablerie (pp. 293–294)

- Drain the victim of all blood, then an **extended Strength roll (diff 9)**;
  each success = 1 automatic aggravated health level on the victim (cannot soak).
- The diablerist is **vulnerable**: all attacks vs them at difficulty 2.
- Success: **Self-Control/Instincts (diff 10 − Humanity/Path)** to avoid losing
  control; if the victim was lower Generation, the diablerist's **Generation
  drops by one permanently**.

mechanics.title: Actions & Turn Sequence
mechanics.content:
# Appendix — Action Resolution: Simple, Extended, Resisted, Reflexive, Multiple, Teamwork (V20 Core)

Source: **V20 Core Rulebook** Chapter Five (pp. 246, 248, 251–253) and Chapter
Six (p. 257). Light format: what each action type is, when to use it, and the
exact resolution rule. The Scholar's own action economy lives here.

## Simple actions (p. 246)

One action = one turn, resolved with one roll; one success is usually enough
(marginal). Anything that could produce an interesting outcome is an action;
speaking and conversation are generally free.

## Reflexive actions (pp. 246, 250)

A significant action that takes no appreciable time and doesn't count as "taking
an action." You may perform **any number** of reflexive actions per turn **with
no penalty**, breaking the normal action sequence as needed. Only requirement:
be conscious/able to choose.

**Examples from the core rules:**
- **Spending blood** to raise an Attribute (no roll, under a second).
- **Soaking** damage from an attack.
- **Humanity / Path rolls** (they may then lead to standard actions).
- **Aborting** to a defensive action (a Willpower roll to abort is reflexive).
- A **Stamina + Survival reflexive roll (difficulty 8)** if the vampire tries to
  heal *while doing other things* (instead of concentrating one full turn).

## Multiple actions (pp. 248, 257)

To do more than one thing in a turn: **declare the total number of actions**,
take the **smallest dice pool among them**, and **divide that many dice among all
the actions** as you see fit.

- **Celerity**: extra actions (up to Celerity dots, 1 BP each) are taken
  **without subtracting dice** from the pools. These extra actions may not
  themselves be split, and must be physical.
- ST discretion: wildly disparate combinations may add a difficulty increase,
  and some splits may be flatly impossible.
- Defensive-only turns: use block/dodge/parry rules instead of splitting (first
  defense full pool, **−1 die cumulative** per subsequent defense in the turn).
- Multiple opponents in close combat: attack **and** defense difficulties +1
  cumulative per extra opponent (max +4).
- Ready a weapon or get to your feet while doing something else = a multiple
  action (Dexterity + Melee/Firearms diff 4 to ready; Dexterity + Athletics diff
  4 to rise).

## Extended actions (pp. 251–252)

Used when a task needs **multiple successes** (more than a marginal success) or
takes longer than one interval. Roll the dice pool **repeatedly at successive
intervals**, accumulating successes toward the target number.

- **The interval is whatever the ST sets** — a turn, an hour, a night, a week
  (e.g., one Wits + Finance roll per night to raise money).
- **A botch** usually forces starting over from scratch (plus a catastrophe),
  and the ST may rule you can't retry at all.
- Extended + resisted: each turn, only the successes **in excess of the rival's
  total** that turn are added to a running tally; first to the target total wins
  (chases, debates, races).

## Resisted actions (p. 252)

Two characters roll against each other; **the most successes wins**, but you only
score **the amount by which you exceed the opponent's successes** (their
successes cancel yours exactly like 1s). So 4 vs 3 = 1 net success (marginal).
The loser's roll still diminishes the winner's result.

- **Difficulty** for a resisted roll is often **one of the opponent's Traits**
  (e.g., difficulty = the target's Willpower).
- Sneaking = Dexterity + Stealth vs Perception + Alertness (both diff 6 unless
  modified).
- Fast-talk = Manipulation + Subterfuge vs target's Willpower (both diff 6).
- Ambush = Dexterity + Stealth vs Perception + Alertness; extra successes add to
  the attacker's attack pool.

## Teamwork (pp. 252–253)

Two or more characters each roll their **own** dice pool (never combine Traits
into one pool) and **add their successes together**. Usually for extended
actions (staking out a target, decoding an inscription, restraining a frenzied
Gangrel, lifting something together).

- **Hindrance** in most social interaction (fast-talking, seducing) — too many
  people overwhelm a single subject.
- **One person's botch can bollix the whole attempt.**

## The four action types (p. 253, summary)

| Type | When | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Simple** | task completes in one roll | ST sets difficulty; roll; automatic success possible |
| **Extended** | a given number of successes needed | roll at intervals, accumulate successes (more botch chances) |
| **Resisted** | a contest of skill | compare successes; most wins, excess only |
| **Extended + Resisted** | a contest needing a target total | running tally of net-successes-per-turn; first to total wins |

## Automatic feats (p. 257)

Things that take an action but normally need no roll: **blood use** (healing,
augmenting Attributes — see blood appendix), **getting to your feet**, **walking/
jogging/running**, **reading a weapon**, **starting a car**, **yielding**.

mechanics.title: Dice & Difficulties
mechanics.content:
# Appendix — Dice Pools, Difficulties & Automatic Success (V20 Core)

Source: **V20 Core Rulebook** Chapter Five: Rules (pp. 245–255). Light format:
pool, difficulty, and effect for each core mechanic. **No example dice** — these
are the Scholar's *own usable* core mechanics, and the fixed rolling convention
is described in the master index header (`SCHOLAR_MECHANICS.md`).

## Rolling dice (v20_core pp. 246–247)

- Vampire uses **10-sided dice**. You roll dice whenever the outcome of an
  action is in doubt; if a roll can't create multiple interesting outcomes, the
  Storyteller should skip it.
- A die result **equal to or greater than the difficulty** is a success. A
  **10 always succeeds**, no matter the difficulty.
- **1s cancel successes** one-for-one. If more 1s than successes and **no**
  successes at all → **botch**. If at least one success was scored, even if
  canceled to net zero, it's a plain **failure**, not a botch.
- **One success** = marginal success (you barely manage). **Three or more** =
  complete success. Degrees: 1 marginal, 2 moderate, 3 complete, 4 exceptional,
  5+ phenomenal.

## Dice pools (p. 247)

- Roll **one die per dot** of the relevant Trait. Most rolls combine an
  **Attribute + Ability** (e.g. Manipulation 3 + Subterfuge 2 = 5 dice).
- Pure rolls (Strength to lift, Humanity to test degeneration, Willpower) use
  the single Trait alone.
- **A dice pool involving a Trait whose max rating is 10 (Humanity, Path,
  Willpower) cannot be combined with any other Trait** — normal characters can
  never roll more than 10 dice.
- The Scholar's standard pools: Attribute + Ability = **10 dice** (all 5s);
  pure Attribute / pure Willpower = **5 dice**.

## Difficulties (pp. 247, 250)

Difficulty is always between 2 and 10 (usually 3–9). **6 is the default** if no
difficulty is given. A 10 result is always a success regardless.

| Difficulty | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Trivial | scanning a small crowd for a familiar face |
| 4 | Easy | following a trail of blood |
| 5 | Straightforward | seducing someone already "in the mood" |
| 6 | Standard (default) | firing a gun |
| 7 | Challenging | locating where the whispers come from |
| 8 | Difficult | convincing a cop it isn't your cocaine |
| 9 | Extremely difficult | walking a tightrope |

At difficulty 10 the probability curve becomes anomalous (botch likelihood can
rise with bigger pools) — assign with care.

## Degrees of success (p. 247)

| Successes | Degree | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Marginal | keeping a broken fridge running until the repairman arrives |
| 2 | Moderate | a handicraft that's ugly but useful |
| 3 | Complete | fixing something good as new |
| 4 | Exceptional | improving efficiency while repairing |
| 5+ | Phenomenal | creating a masterwork |

## Failure (p. 249)

Zero net successes = the action fails. Failure is *just* failure — the attempt
didn't produce the desired result; it doesn't automatically hurt the character
unless circumstances say otherwise.

## Botches (pp. 249–250)

Botch = **no successes AND one or more 1s**. A botch is dramatic misfortune,
ruled by the Storyteller (dropped gun, enraged animal, revealing a lie, a chase
gone wrong). Optional: the ST may give everyone one "free" botch per session
that doesn't count.

## Automatic success (p. 250)

- If **dice pool ≥ difficulty**, the character succeeds automatically **without
  rolling** — for mundane tasks only. **Never works in combat or other
  stressful situations.** It counts as a marginal (1-success) result; you may
  still roll to chase extra successes.
- **Willpower**: spending **1 Willpower point** grants **1 automatic success**
  on a single roll. Once per turn. The success **cannot be canceled, even by
  botches** (1s). Must be declared **before** rolling; cannot be used to
  retroactively cancel a botch. The ST may disallow it on certain actions
  (e.g., attacking in combat).
- A **10** may also count as 2 successes if the action falls within the
  character's **specialty** (p. 96).

## Trying it again (p. 251)

Failed a roll you may retry? Then each subsequent attempt in the same endeavor
suffers **+1 difficulty** (first retry +1, second +2, etc.) until impossible.
ST discretion: doesn't apply to stress-situations (missing a gunshot, failing to
detect an ambush), where retries are expected.

## Ratings (p. 247)

Traits are rated in **dots 1–5** (0 = never learned; some exceptions like a
Nosferatu's Appearance). 1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 4 exceptional, 5 superb.

## Time units (p. 254)

- **Turn** — 3 seconds to ~3 minutes, one simple action.
- **Scene** — action at one location; as many turns as it takes.
- **Chapter** — one game-session segment; scenes linked by downtime.
- **Story** — a full tale (may span chapters).
- **Chronicle** — the connected series of stories.
- **Downtime** — time glossed over with description rather than played turn by
  turn.

## Skill defaulting (p. 257)

For rolls using **Talents and Skills**, a character lacking the Ability may
**default to the base Attribute**, but **Skill-based actions are at +1
difficulty**. (Knowledges can't be defaulted.)

mechanics.title: Social & Influence Rolls
mechanics.content:
# Appendix — Social Rolls & Social Combat (V20 Core)

Source: **V20 Core Rulebook** Chapter Six: Systems and Drama, pp. 263–266 (Social
Feats), plus the resisted-action rules from Chapter Five (p. 252). Light format:
pool, difficulty, resisted-vs, and effect. **Roleplaying supersedes rolls** — the
rules are a fallback when a social moment is genuinely in doubt.

## General principles (pp. 263, 252)

- Social tasks use a **Social Attribute + Ability** pool, usually resisted
  against a target Trait (most often **Willpower**).
- **Resisted action**: net successes = your successes minus the opponent's;
  extra successes often add detail/leverage.
- If **extra successes exceed the target's permanent Willpower**, the target
  "folds completely" (full confession, total submission, etc.).
- **Teamwork hurts** most social attempts (too many cooks overwhelm one subject).
- On a botch the character looks foolish/credible-loss; the ST rules the
  outcome.

## Social feats (pp. 263–266)

### Carousing — Charisma + Empathy
Difficulty typically **6** (higher for large/surly groups; certain Natures
adjust it). Relax targets, loosen tongues, make instant allies. Botch = you come
off as an obnoxious boor (people wonder why you never touch food/drink).

### Credibility — Manipulation + Subterfuge (perpetrate) / Perception + Subterfuge (detect)
Scam or detect one (impersonation, forged papers, false credentials).
Difficulty typically **7** for both sides; the "marks" must roll higher than the
perpetrator to detect the deception. Props/forgeries raise the difficulty of
uncovering it; teamwork can help reveal it. Botch = the plan falls apart.

### Fast-Talk — Manipulation + Subterfuge vs target's Willpower
**Resisted** (both difficulty **6**); whoever scores more successes wins. Tie =
more babbling needed. Botch = you anger the target and ramble to no effect.

### Interrogation
- **Peaceful (Manipulation + Empathy)** — resisted vs the subject's Willpower
  (both diff **6**). Rolls at key points of questioning.
- **Violent (Manipulation + Intimidation)** — resisted vs the target's
  **Stamina + 3 or Willpower (whichever is higher)**. Physical torture costs the
  subject **1 health level per turn**; mental torture **1 temporary WP per
  turn**; both together is devastating. Botch can destroy the subject's body or
  mind.
- Two interrogators may combine successes (good cop/bad cop works even mixing
  Empathy and Intimidation). Extra successes = additional revealed information;
  exceeding the victim's permanent Willpower = full confession.

### Intimidation — Manipulation + Intimidation, or Strength + Intimidation
- **Passive**: no roll; higher Intimidation = wider berth in public.
- **Subtle** (perceived threat): **Manipulation + Intimidation** resisted vs the
  subject's **Willpower** (both diff **6**); the subject must beat your successes
  or be cowed.
- **Blatant** (direct physical threat): **Strength + Intimidation** (diff **6**)
  resisted vs the subject's **Willpower or Strength + Intimidation (higher)**.
  Botch = you look patently ridiculous for the rest of the scene.

### Oration — Charisma + Leadership
Difficulty typically **6**, raised for huge/cynical/hostile audiences. Hit or
miss. Preparing a speech (Intelligence + Expression, diff 7) lowers the oration
difficulty by 1 on success (raises it on a botch).

### Performance — Charisma + Performance
Difficulty **7** (raised by audience mood / complexity). 1 success = enjoyable
but uninspired; more = truly memorable. Botch = forgotten lines, wrong chord,
flub.

### Seduction — three-stage resisted process
1. **Approach** — Appearance + Subterfuge vs difficulty (subject's **Wits + 3**);
   each success beyond the first adds a die to the next roll.
2. **Witty repartee** — Wits + Subterfuge vs difficulty (subject's
   **Intelligence + 3**); each success beyond the first adds a die to the final
   roll.
3. **Intimate conversation** — Charisma + Empathy vs difficulty (subject's
   **Perception + 3**); success = the subject is enamored and goes somewhere
   private.

Botch at any stage usually ends with a drink in the vampire's face.

## Example social rolls (p. 255)

- Dexterity + Etiquette (diff 8) — flawless manners at a formal dinner.
- Charisma + Intimidation, resisted by the rival's Charisma + Intimidation —
  a glare-off with the gang leader.
- Manipulation + Intimidation (diff 8) — a veiled threat at Elysium.
- Perception + Intimidation (diff 5) — reading whether a Lick just threatened you.
- Manipulation + Expression, resisted by a rival's Manipulation + Expression —
  whose story the Prince believes.
- Charisma + Law (diff 8) — pleading for release before sunrise.
- Charisma + Streetwise (diff 8) — picking up word on a new gang (extended, one
  roll per night).

## Social conflict at scale

- **Extended + resisted** social contests (a long seduction, a debate before
  assembled Elysium, a cat-and-mouse negotiation): net-successes-per-turn are
  tallied; the first to the target total wins (p. 252).
- **Blood bond / Presence leverage**: a 2-drink bond makes social rolls vs the
  thrall at **−1 difficulty**; a full bond allows Dominate by voice alone and
  mental-control resistance at **+2 difficulty** (see the damage/blood appendix).
- **Derangement effects** (from the states-of-being section, pp. 290–293) modify
  social rolls: **Paranoia** adds +1 difficulty to all interaction rolls;
  **Megalomania** adds an extra die to all Willpower rolls; **Schizophrenia**
  adds +3 difficulty to frenzy-resistance rolls and removes 3 dice from all
  Willpower rolls.
